correctness.rationale: In the regular differential basis (dx/y, dx/y², x dx/y²), parity and the two cubic characters make the Cartier matrix diagonal for p=6m+1. The first two basis vectors are anti-invariant and the third is invariant. Expanding around z=−a/2 and using Lucas gives D^m dividing B and F, where D=a²−4b; degree and specialization at b=0 give F. B is also divisible by b^m, coprime to D^m. Substitution of B=b^mD^m Q into its coefficient ODE makes the Q' multiplier (4m−1)a and the Q multiplier −3m² mod p, exactly the equation for H. The leading indicial factor −(d−m)(d−3m) is nonzero for degrees d<m, proving quotient uniqueness and the stated leading-coefficient ratio. At b=1 the boundary evaluations are nonzero. A repeated root elsewhere of order r would give leading ODE term (4−a₀²)r(r−1) times a nonzero coefficient, impossible for 2≤r≤m<p. The elliptic Cartier scalar is a unit on the smooth locus. The degree-four isogeny separates the p-divisible groups, so simultaneous vanishing of the two Prym entries gives a=2 (superspecial) and simultaneous nonvanishing gives ordinary. Normalization leaves a sign action; the root at zero is present exactly for odd m. Independent exact polynomial-multiplication and gcd checks at p=7,13,19,37,97 replay with python3 /workspace/review-evidence/reproduce.py 3 (SymPy). These are finite corroboration; the supplied checker was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The count is geometric and marked; it says nothing about root fields or a rational isogeny census. The root separability statement concerns the normalized coefficient line, not a claim about a coarse quotient scheme's multiplicities.
